title: Telescope Mount Guiding Error Trend
dataSources: Observatory environment (`observatory:env`), sky-quality meter (`skyquality:reading`), imaging sessions (`imaging:session`), telescope mount (`mount:status`), cloud sensor (`allsky:cloud`).
app: Backyard observatory automation — roll-off-roof/dome controller, sky-quality meter, cloud sensor, telescope mount, and astrophotography capture software (N.I.N.A./Ekos) — logging to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=mount:status
| timechart span=5m avg(guide_rms_arcsec) as rms
| eval poor=if(rms>1.5,1,0)
description: Trends your mount's guiding error so you can see when wind, balance, or a cable snag is blurring your exposures.
value: Guiding error directly sets your sharpness limit; watching it live lets you abort and fix a bad run instead of wasting the night.
implementation: Ingest guiding RMS from your imaging software; review the trend and flag periods of poor tracking.
visualization: Time chart of guiding error with a quality threshold.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks how steadily your telescope tracks the stars, so you can spot when something is making your photos blurry.
